\markboth{IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON PARALLEL AND DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS,~Vol.~XX, No.~X, Month~YYYY}%
{Patel \MakeLowercase{\textit{et~al.}}: Bitwise-Reproducible Reduction Across Cluster Reshape}

{%
\vspace{2mm}\begingroup\sffamily\small\color{spInk}\textcolor{spBlue}{\textbf{Abstract}}\par\vspace{1mm}
Floating-point reductions are not bitwise reproducible under \emph{cluster
reshape}: change the worker count or the network and the collective changes its
reduction order, and with it the last bits. We measure that premise rather than
assert it --- reducing identical input \emph{bytes} at \GpuWorldSizes{} rank
counts under PyTorch's collectives returns \GpuRootsDistinct{} distinct 64-bit
roots with spreads reaching \GpuUlpMax{}~ulp, while repeats at a fixed shape are
bitwise identical. Reduction order is therefore an \emph{interface} concern, and
we treat it as a compiler/fabric ABI: a size-indexed contract fixing the operand
binding at every internal node of a canonical full binary tree $\FBT(N)$. No
conjunct is ours alone; the conjunction is --- invariance across network
\emph{topologies} rather than resource counts alone, an unmodified IEEE-754 FP64
operator with no wide accumulator, arbitrary non-power-of-two $N$, and
enforcement below the software stack, so that a violated assumption fail-stops
instead of returning a quietly different number. We instantiate the ABI as
\sprs{}, a topology-parametric SystemVerilog NoC plus compiler, and state a
cross-topology bitwise invariance claim and a presence-gated fail-stop property,
connected by a mapping/topology orthogonality proposition. Enumerating the
refinement-free face of the compiler's configuration space exhaustively on the
\TournNInst{} hardware-validated members of a \SuiteSize{}-instance suite
spanning $N\!\in\![8,8192]$, $G\!\in\![2,4096]$ and six direct networks, \WallTBs{} of
\InvAttempted{} distinct program images settled in RTL simulation and every
one returned the canonical root; \InvNonSettling{} did not settle, all but one a fabric watchdog
fail-stop, and no run returned a finite root differing from it. Injected faults
establish oracle non-vacuity on \MutOracleLo{}--\MutOracleHi{} of \MutTotal{}
verdicts. The compiler's search space provably cannot reach the bit result;
what it can reach is a fixed portfolio of \SelConfigsRun{} of
\SelConfigsTotal{} configurations that attains the measured optimum on
\SelKFourOpt{} of \TournNInst{} held-out instances and transfers to a withheld
topology, beating every rule we could fit that conditions on the instance.
Finally we export the discipline to production collectives in software
(\emph{pinned-FBT}), correct the natural index-range construction, and
price the repair: bitwise reshape-invariant on all \PinCells{} cells swept
against a negative control that fires, at a geometric mean of $\PinCostGeo\times$
stock \texttt{ncclAllReduce} --- provisional under GPU contention, of which
about a factor of two is algorithmic, in bytes moved.
\endgroup\vspace{3mm}

\section{The Problem}\label{sec:intro}
% =====================================================================

\IEEEPARstart{P}{roduction} all-reduce implementations --- ring, recursive
halving--doubling, double-binary tree --- pick the reduction order that
maximises throughput for the observed topology and worker
count~\cite{rabenseifner2004optimization,nccl2018}. When either changes, so
does the order. IEEE~754 addition is non-associative, so the order is part of
the answer: for two orders $\sigma,\sigma'$ of the same
multiset~\cite{higham2002accuracy},
\begin{equation}
  \bigl|\,{\textstyle\sum_\sigma x_i} - {\textstyle\sum_{\sigma'} x_i}\,\bigr|
  \;\leq\; (N-1)\,u\,{\textstyle\sum_i} |x_i| + \mathcal{O}(u^2),
  \label{eq:higham}
\end{equation}
a bound that is catastrophically loose under cancellation, and whose
consequences are documented across HPC and deep-learning
workloads~\cite{shanmugavelu2024}.

The consequence is measured in \S\ref{sec:results-premise}, not asserted:
reducing identical input \emph{bytes} at \GpuWorldSizes{} rank counts under
PyTorch's distributed collectives~\cite{li2020pytorch} --- same data, same
seed, same code, only the shape of the job changing --- returns
\GpuRootsDistinct{} distinct 64-bit results, while repeated runs at any
\emph{fixed} shape are bitwise identical \GpuRepeats{} times out of
\GpuRepeats{}. Reshape moves the answer; noise does not. In a training loop
the divergence compounds: the reduced gradient becomes the next step's
weights. Bit-for-bit regression testing fails the same way --- a code accepted
on a development cluster produces different last bits on the production
cluster, and the reviewer cannot separate a new bug from the reshape
artefact. In regulated deployments, inability to replay a computation bitwise
across hardware generations is increasingly disqualifying.

Two sources produce this. \emph{Order-dependence of the reducer}: NCCL selects
its (algorithm, protocol) pair at communicator initialisation from a cost
model over architecture, node and rank counts and message
size~\cite{nccl2018}; the data are never consulted, so with all randomness
suppressed the algorithm remains a deterministic function of
$(G,\text{topology})$. \emph{Reassociation inside the reducer}: pipeline
overlap, SIMD lanes and message merging are each an implicit reassociation.
Both have been attacked before, along one axis at a time
(\S\ref{sec:related}).

What no line of work states is the invariant \emph{at the interface}, enforced
below the software that could violate it. A library flag cannot forbid
Source~1, because the library has no authority over what cluster size is
launched tomorrow; a fabric guarantee alone cannot forbid Source~2, because
the fabric cannot see the tree a scheduler intends. The discipline has to be a
contract shared by both. The principle is not new --- IEEE~754-2019 already
makes reproducibility an obligation on language processors, forbidding
reordering and fusion under its \emph{reproducible}
attribute~\cite{ieee754-2019} --- but that obligation binds within one
program and says nothing about how many workers run a collective or how they
are wired. We extend it to the interface the standard does not reach, and
index it by problem size so that it survives a change of deployment.

\emph{Contributions.} \textbf{(C1)} Reduction order as a size-indexed
compiler/fabric ABI, with a structural invariance argument
(\S\ref{sec:abi}): Claim~\ref{claim:1} (cross-topology bitwise invariance)
and Property~\ref{prop:2} (presence-gated fail-stop), connected by
Proposition~\ref{thm:orth}. We claim the framing, not the difficulty of the proof: once
operand binding is a function of tree-node identity alone, invariance follows
by unwinding definitions, and we say so rather than dressing it as a
discovery. The work is in the three places the proof does not reach ---
building a fabric that enforces the binding with no silently-wrong failure
mode, establishing that every remaining degree of freedom in a real compiler
is orthogonal to it, and carrying the discipline onto a production collective
and paying its price. \textbf{(C2)} A fabric (\S\ref{sec:fabric}) and compiler
(\S\ref{sec:compiler}) that jointly realise it, in which topology is a runtime
table rather than an RTL artefact and one compiler pass \emph{constructs} the
single-writer discipline the argument needs. \textbf{(C3)} A hardware campaign
at scale and a structural pricing of the ABI (\S\S\ref{sec:method},
\ref{sec:results}), plus a software export onto production collectives
(\S\ref{sec:pinfbt}). What is \emph{not} claimed: interoperability with any
external reducer, strict IEEE~754 (\S\ref{sec:fadd}), silicon timing, or novel
component algorithms --- our eighteen assignment and ten mapping algorithms
are prior art~\cite{topcuoglu2002heft,lukes1974efficient,dally2004principles};
the observation is that any choice among them inherits invariance by
composition.

\emph{Roadmap.} \S\ref{sec:background} fixes the threat model and places the
work against prior reproducibility approaches. \S\ref{sec:abi} is the
contract: canonical tree, operand binding, the fifteen assumptions,
Claim~\ref{claim:1}, Property~\ref{prop:2} and the orthogonality proposition.
\S\ref{sec:fabric} is the hardware that establishes the fabric-side
invariants and \S\ref{sec:compiler} the compiler that discharges the
compiler-side obligations. \S\S\ref{sec:method}--\ref{sec:results} are the
campaign in which the two are run together; \S\ref{sec:pinfbt} carries the
same discipline onto production collectives in software and prices it there;
\S\ref{sec:discussion} is the analysis, scope and generalisation.




% =====================================================================
\section{Background and Threat Model}\label{sec:background}
% =====================================================================

\emph{Where the order comes from.} Let $\tau$ be a binary reduction tree over
$N$ binary64 values and $\Sigma_\tau$ the 64-bit result of evaluating it with
RNE rounding at every internal node. Equation~\eqref{eq:higham} is loose
generically and tight under cancellation: when the exact sum is small
relative to the partial sums, $\Sigma_\tau$ and $\Sigma_{\tau'}$ can differ
at the exponent scale of the largest partial sum rather than of the result.
Production collectives choose $\tau$ from the deployment.
Ring all-reduce~\cite{patarasuk2009bandwidth} orders along a physical worker
ring; recursive halving--doubling~\cite{rabenseifner2004optimization} orders
by a power-of-two recursive pattern; double-binary-tree
all-reduce~\cite{sanders2009two} interleaves two trees; runtime-hybrid
libraries~\cite{nccl2018,rccl2019} select among these per message size from
topology discovered at communicator initialisation. In each case $\tau$ is a
function of $(G,\text{topology},\text{message size})$ and never of the data,
so reshaping the cluster reshapes $\tau$ and therefore $\Sigma_\tau$. The
same dependence is documented for MPI reduction
operations~\cite{balaji2013reproducible}.

\begin{definition}[Cross-topology bitwise reproducibility]\label{def:ctbr}
Let $L \in (\mathrm{bits}_{64})^N$ be a fixed leaf-value vector. For every
$(G,\text{topology})$ with topology in $\T$, every valid \sprs{} compilation
and every valid execution of the fabric, the observed 64-bit root is the same
sequence of bits.
\end{definition}

$\T$ is the family of flat direct networks realisable by a configuration of
the per-router adjacency and routing tables: linear, ring, 2D mesh, 2D torus,
hypercube and fat-tree. Definition~\ref{def:ctbr} is \emph{structural} --- a
statement about what the compiler/fabric pair can be shown to guarantee, not
an empirical average over executions --- which is why the evaluation reports
a divergence count rather than a divergence rate.

Four things are deliberately outside it. (i) Agreement between \sprs{} and an
external reducer that fixes a different canonical order. (ii) Tolerance to
single-event upsets or transient faults. (iii) Portability of bit patterns
between fabrics with different FADD microarchitectures. (iv) Adversarial or
merely unlucky traffic patterns affecting \emph{cycle counts}; these cannot
affect the bit result, and \S\ref{sec:noc-route} says what they can affect.

Table~\ref{tab:prior} classifies the field along those two sources. Two
groups already deliver invariance under a change of resource count and we do
not claim otherwise: order-independent accumulators do it by changing the
operator, and fixed-order schemes do it with the operator intact but each
within one library and along one axis. What no row other than the last
combines is invariance across network \emph{topologies} rather than resource
counts alone, an unmodified FP64 operator, arbitrary non-power-of-two $N$,
and enforcement below the software stack with a fail-stop failure mode.
\S\ref{sec:related} treats the rows individually.


% =====================================================================
\section{The Reduction ABI}\label{sec:abi}
% =====================================================================

\subsection{The Canonical Tree}\label{sec:abi-tree}

\begin{definition}[Canonical full binary tree]\label{def:fbt}
For $N \geq 1$, $\FBT(N)$ is the heap-indexed binary tree with $2N-1$ nodes:
root at index $0$, children of $i$ at $2i+1$ and $2i+2$; internal nodes
$\{0,\ldots,N-2\}$, leaves $\{N-1,\ldots,2N-2\}$. Since $2N-1$ is odd, every
internal node has exactly two children: the single-child edge case is
eliminated at the tree level.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Canonical leaf enumeration]\label{def:leafenum}
$\mathrm{idx}$ assigns index $k$ to the $k$-th smallest \emph{heap index} in
the leaf set of $\FBT(N)$.
\end{definition}

Definition~\ref{def:leafenum} needs stating precisely because the obvious
paraphrase is wrong. Ascending heap index and left-to-right \emph{visual}
order coincide exactly when $N$ is a power of two. Otherwise $\FBT(N)$ is
depth-imbalanced and a shallower leaf carries a \emph{smaller} heap index than
deeper leaves to its left: for $N=7$ the heap order is
$\langle 6,\ldots,12\rangle$ while visual order is
$\langle 7,\ldots,12,6\rangle$. Seven of the sixteen leaf counts we evaluate
are of this shape, and at $N=200$ the two enumerations give roots differing by
one ulp. An implementation using visual order implements a \emph{different}
contract.

Write $\pi_N$ for the post-order traversal of $\FBT(N)$ restricted to internal
nodes --- a pure function of $N$; $\pi_4 = \langle 1,2,0\rangle$. The
canonical evaluation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Rcan}
  \Rcan(N, L) \;=\; \mathrm{evaluate}\bigl(\FBT(N), L, \fadd\bigr),
\end{equation}
with $L$ indexed by $\mathrm{idx}$ and $\fadd$ the combinational semantics of
our FP64 adder (\S\ref{sec:fadd}). Equation~\eqref{eq:Rcan} is the
\emph{target} of every \sprs{} execution on $(N,L)$.

\emph{The canonical order is a constraint, not a tautology.} One might suspect
that any association order yields one root per $N$, so agreement across
topologies measures nothing. We measured how far that is from true. On the
leaf vectors evaluated here, right-to-left sequential summation differs from
$\Rcan$ by up to \OrderUlpMax{} ulp at $N = \OrderUlpMaxN$, and left-to-right
differs at \OrderLRDiff{} of the sixteen leaf counts. The discriminating power
is strongly $N$-dependent and not monotone: exhaustively at $N=8$, all
\OrderPermsEight{} leaf permutations yield only \OrderRootsEight{} distinct
roots, \OrderCanonPctEight{} of them the canonical one, so a uniformly random
leaf-order violation is detected with probability \OrderDetectEight{}; at
$N=16$, all \OrderShapesSixteen{} in-order tree shapes yield
\OrderRootsSixteen{} distinct roots spanning two ulp. Across the sixteen leaf
counts the probability that a sampled reassociation moves the root ranges from
\OrderProbMin{} to \OrderProbMax{}. Two consequences follow and we adopt both:
the oracle is non-vacuous, so an agreeing run is evidence; and the rows of the
invariance table are not equally informative --- at small $N$ agreement is
close to free, and the weight of the evidence sits at the large leaf counts.

\subsection{The ABI}\label{sec:abi-def}

\begin{definition}[Operand binding]\label{def:opbind}
For every internal node $v$ of $\FBT(N)$ the compiler emits exactly one
\texttt{COMPUTE} on the PE hosting $v$, with
$\mathtt{addr\_a} = \mathrm{dmem}(\mathrm{left}(v))$ and
$\mathtt{addr\_b} = \mathrm{dmem}(\mathrm{right}(v))$, where
$\mathrm{dmem}(\cdot)$ is a per-PE address assigned by the allocator. The
binding is a pure function of $v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Leaf binding]\label{def:leafbind}
For every leaf $k$, the \texttt{GENERATE} on the PE hosting $k$ writes
$L[\mathrm{idx}(k)]$ into the DMEM slot bound to $k$.
\end{definition}

The fabric executes the two disciplines symmetrically: \texttt{COMPUTE} reads
both DMEM slots at one clock edge, scoreboard-gated, and writes
$\fadd(\cdot,\cdot)$; \texttt{GENERATE} delivers $L[\mathrm{idx}(k)]$ with the
scoreboard set. Neither discipline references $G$, topology, assignment
$\asgn$, mapping $\map$, refinement $r$, or timing. These are left free
precisely so that schedulers may keep optimising without touching the
contract, and they are what the campaign of \S\ref{sec:method} searches over.

\subsection{Assumptions}\label{sec:abi-assumptions}

Fifteen assumptions carry the two properties: five \emph{compiler obligations}
(\textsf{C-*}), discharged by the compiler or the user, and ten \emph{fabric
invariants} (\textsf{F-*}), established by RTL inspection. Eleven are
hypotheses of Claim~\ref{claim:1}; the four marked~$\dagger$ are liveness
invariants that can stop a run but cannot alter a root the fabric does
produce, and are the hypotheses of Property~\ref{prop:2} instead.
The supplemental material states all fifteen. The partition is not
cosmetic: the \textsf{C-*} obligations are post-conditions on the emitted
image, checkable without executing anything, while the \textsf{F-*} invariants
are properties of the fabric independent of any compilation --- so a failure
of Claim~\ref{claim:1} is diagnosable as a compiler bug or an RTL bug, not
both.

Three conditions a reader might expect are absent. \emph{Compilation
determinism} is not a hypothesis: Claim~\ref{claim:1} quantifies over every
image the compiler can emit, and a statement true of all of them does not need
the compiler to be a function of its seed. \emph{Partition connectedness} is
not either, although \DisconnCount{} of the RTL-validated configurations
(\DisconnShare{}) have partitions that are not connected subtrees: operand
binding is by node identity and every cross-PE child gets a dedicated receive
slot, so the emitted binding is $(\mathrm{left}(v),\mathrm{right}(v))$ for
\emph{any} assignment --- checked statically on \BindComputes{}
\texttt{COMPUTE} and \BindSends{} \texttt{SEND} instructions across
\BindConfigs{} configurations, with \BindViolations{} violations. What
disconnection costs is DMEM occupancy, and that is what \textsf{C-mem} bounds.
The \emph{identity slot} \texttt{DMEM[0]} is reserved but unread here, since
$\FBT(N)$ has no single-child internal node.

\begin{remark}[The \textsf{C-mem} margin, and what lies past it]
\label{rem:cmem}
\textsf{C-mem} is the one hypothesis of Claim~\ref{claim:1} the campaign came
close to violating, so we report the margin rather than the fact of
compliance. Peak DMEM occupancy over the validated configurations reaches
\DmemPeakMax{} of \DmemDepth{} slots, a margin of \DmemMargin. Past the
ceiling the claim fails, and it fails \emph{silently}: on a constructed
$\FBT(\DmemCexLeaves)$ instance at $G = \DmemCexWorkers$ with all leaves on
one PE, peak occupancy is \DmemCexPeak{} slots, \DmemCexOver{} emitted
addresses exceed the depth, and the run terminates normally --- no
\texttt{P\_ERROR}, no deadlock --- returning a wrong root, and two
\emph{different} wrong roots under two different packet-delivery orders.
Aliasing defeats the presence gate rather than tripping it, because the
aliased slot has been written by something. The fabric cannot detect the
condition, which is why \textsf{C-mem} is a hypothesis of Claim~\ref{claim:1}
rather than a property of the machine. The compiler can: the emitter now
carries a post-condition over the instruction words it is about to write and
raises \sv{EmitRefused} rather than emit an image whose addresses would
alias, so the failure above is a recorded compile failure in the released
tool and a wrong root only in the version we measured it on. No configuration
in the campaign trips that post-condition, which is the same statement as the
margin.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Claim 1 and the Fail-Stop Property}\label{sec:abi-claim}

\begin{claim}[Cross-topology bitwise invariance]\label{claim:1}
Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L \in (\mathrm{bits}_{64})^N$ be a fixed
leaf-value vector, and let $\T$ be the family of flat direct-network
topologies realisable by adjacency tables consistent with
\sv{noc\_system.sv}. Assume \textsf{C-sw}, \textsf{C-bind}, \textsf{C-leaf},
\textsf{C-mem} and \textsf{F-sb-mono}, \textsf{F-sb-gate}, \textsf{F-fw},
\textsf{F-inorder}, \textsf{F-gci-haz}, \textsf{F-arb}, \textsf{F-fadd}. Let
$G$ be a worker count and $\tau \in \T$ a topology for which the compiler
emits an image satisfying \textsf{C-mem}; let $\asgn$, $\map$, $r$ be any
valid assignment, mapping and refinement, and $s$ the emitted per-PE schedule.
If the run terminates normally --- \sv{all\_done} asserted, no
\texttt{P\_ERROR}, no watchdog --- then the observed 64-bit root, the result
of the root PE's final \texttt{COMPUTE}, satisfies
\begin{equation}
  R_\mathrm{observed}(N, L, G, \tau, \asgn, \map, r, s)
    \;=\; \Rcan(N, L).
\end{equation}
\end{claim}

Three features of the statement bind a reimplementer. \emph{First},
\textsf{C-mem} is a compilability precondition, not a decoration: the claim
asserts nothing about a configuration whose image exceeds the per-PE DMEM
budget or whose router count exceeds what the adjacency interface can address.
One instance in our suite is in that position, and it is also the one that
never settles (\S\ref{sec:limitations}). \emph{Second}, the claim is
partial-correctness; liveness is Property~\ref{prop:2}'s business, which is
exactly why \textsf{C-route}, \textsf{F-credit}, \textsf{F-misroute} and
\textsf{F-watchdog} are not hypotheses here. \emph{Third}, the observable is
the root PE's final \texttt{COMPUTE} result, not the root DMEM slot, which no
emitted instruction ever reads back.

\begin{property}[Presence-gated fail-stop]\label{prop:2}
Suppose an assumption violation causes some \texttt{COMPUTE} to name a DMEM
address whose presence bit is never set --- a misrouted and dropped packet
(\textsf{F-misroute}), a lost credit (\textsf{F-credit}), an unreachable
destination (\textsf{C-route}), or an operand bound to a slot no agent writes
(\textsf{C-bind}). Then no instruction retires on the affected PE,
\textsf{F-watchdog} fires after $\sv{WATCHDOG\_MAX} = \WatchdogMax$
consecutive non-retiring cycles, and the PE enters \texttt{P\_ERROR} recording
\sv{error\_pc} and \sv{error\_state}; \sv{all\_done} is never asserted and no
root is produced. An invalid opcode raises \texttt{P\_ERROR} immediately.
\end{property}

The converse bound is equally explicit, because the property is easy to
over-read. The fabric checks presence, not identity: a \texttt{COMPUTE} whose
operands are both present executes, whatever they contain. Violations leaving
every read address present --- an operand misbound to a live slot, a corrupted
leaf value, a duplicate write to a receive buffer, an over-budget image in
which two addresses alias onto one written slot, or a violation of any of the
seven safety \textsf{F-*} invariants --- terminate normally with a wrong root.
The fabric does not detect these and we do not claim it does; they are
discharged by the compile-time post-condition on the emitted image and by
comparison of the final root against the oracle.

\emph{How the hypotheses carry the claim.} Four steps, each of the eleven
used at least once. \emph{Addresses} (\textsf{C-bind}, \textsf{C-mem}):
\sv{build\_schedule} binds a \texttt{COMPUTE}'s operands from an address map
keyed on node identity, and every cross-PE child holds a dedicated receive
slot, so the emitted binding is $(\mathrm{left}(v),\mathrm{right}(v))$ under
any assignment; \textsf{C-mem} is what promotes that address-level statement
to a value-level one, since the fabric truncates addresses and distinct
addresses stay distinct only while the image fits DMEM. \emph{Uniqueness}
(\textsf{C-sw}, \textsf{F-sb-mono}): $\FBT(N)$ is a tree, so each node has one
consumer; the allocator therefore gives each receive buffer exactly one
writer, and its scoreboard bit transitions $0\to1$ exactly once per program.
\emph{Values} (\textsf{F-sb-gate}, \textsf{F-fw}, \textsf{F-inorder},
\textsf{F-gci-haz}, \textsf{F-arb}): every address a \texttt{COMPUTE} reads is
a receive buffer or a local temporary. For the first, \textsf{F-sb-gate} holds
the instruction in \textsf{DE} until both bits are set, so at the EX edge both
slots hold their committed remote writes, with \textsf{F-fw} closing the
BRAM read-first race. For the second the scoreboard is silent --- a recycled
slot's bit is already set --- and need not speak: under \textsf{F-inorder} the
overwriting \texttt{COMPUTE} samples its operands strictly before writeback,
and the one writer program order does not sequence, an in-flight
\texttt{GENERATE}, is covered by \textsf{F-gci-haz} and its retry latch
\textsf{F-arb}. \emph{Function} (\textsf{F-fadd}): the committed value is
$\fadd$ of those stable inputs, a pure function. Composing, every internal
DMEM value at termination is $\fadd$ applied to $v$'s two children --- with
leaves supplied by \textsf{C-leaf} --- so the root PE's final \texttt{COMPUTE}
returns $\mathrm{evaluate}(\FBT(N), L, \fadd) = \Rcan(N,L)$, in which no free
axis appears.

We label these a \emph{claim} and a \emph{property} rather than theorems
because the supporting argument proceeds by RTL inspection, a compiler
post-condition, end-to-end root comparison and mutation testing, not by formal
proof (\S\ref{sec:limitations}, L1).

\subsection{Mapping/Topology Orthogonality}\label{sec:abi-orth}

Of the axes Claim~\ref{claim:1} quantifies over, $(G,\asgn)$ is where the
substantive work lives: changing $G$ changes the number of PEs and changing
$\asgn$ changes which PE hosts which node. The $(\text{topology},\map,\rho,s)$
slice admits a sharper statement.

\begin{proposition}[Mapping/topology orthogonality]\label{thm:orth}
Fix $N$, $L$, $\asgn$, $r$ and the FADD unit. For any two valid mappings
$\map_1,\map_2$ and any two valid routing tables $\rho_1,\rho_2$ for
(possibly different) topologies in $\T$,
\begin{equation}
  R_\mathrm{observed}(\map_1, \rho_1) = R_\mathrm{observed}(\map_2, \rho_2)
  = \Rcan(N, L).
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{structuralargument}
By inspection of \sv{build\_schedule} and \sv{generate\_instructions}: a
\texttt{COMPUTE}'s $(\texttt{addr\_a},\texttt{addr\_b},\texttt{dest})$ triple
depends only on $\asgn$ and the DMEM allocator's output, neither of which
reads $\map$ or the routing tables. A \texttt{SEND}'s
$(\texttt{dest\_gpu},\texttt{target\_addr},\text{link})$ triple does depend on
$\map$ and on routing, but those determine only \emph{where} data flows, not
the operand binding at the receiving PE. Under \textsf{F-sb-gate} the
receiving \texttt{COMPUTE} reads DMEM by address, not by arrival time, port or
VC. Hence $R_\mathrm{observed}$ is independent of $(\map,\rho)$.
\end{structuralargument}

Proposition~\ref{thm:orth} is the cleanest statement of what the ABI buys: the
two things that change most obviously under cluster reshape are structurally
orthogonal to the bit result. This is a consequence of the code path that
emits the instructions, not a hypothesis to be validated empirically.

\subsection{FADD Policy}\label{sec:fadd}

Our adder (\sv{fp64\_add.sv}, with a bit-exact Python mirror) implements a
\emph{deterministic subset} of IEEE~754-2019 binary64 addition, which we
specify fully as \emph{FTZ+RNE}: subnormal inputs flushed to $\pm0$ preserving
sign; round-to-nearest-even only, with no rounding-mode register; post-round
subnormals flushed likewise; $x+(-x) = +0$ and $(-0)+(-0) = +0$ (a documented
deviation from \S6.3 of the standard); a quieted qNaN whose sign and payload
are taken from $a$ when $a$ is NaN and from $b$ otherwise; and the usual
infinity rules with $\pm\infty + \mp\infty$ returning the canonical qNaN.
Invariance depends only on $\fadd$ being a pure function of its inputs, not on
any particular IEEE~754 feature; a subnormal-aware alternative inherits
Claim~\ref{claim:1} by construction. The subset is checked rather than
asserted: the shipped adder shows \FpSweepErrors{} disagreements with
correctly-rounded IEEE~754 addition over \FpSweepVectors{} vectors inside the
documented scope. The adder we first submitted did not meet the RNE clause on
effective subtraction. \S\ref{sec:fabric-fadd} reports the defect and its
repair, and \S\ref{sec:limitations} (L13) reports why neither the campaign
nor the software mirror could have found it --- a finding about the
evaluation method rather than an erratum.


% =====================================================================
\section{The Fabric}\label{sec:fabric}
% =====================================================================

The fabric establishes the \textsf{F-*} invariants. It supports up to $4096$
PEs in a single Verilog instantiation, and four properties carry the ABI into
hardware: topology is a runtime configuration rather than an RTL artefact
(\S\ref{sec:fabric-topo}); the ISA is small enough to audit for ABI adherence
(\S\ref{sec:fabric-isa}); the scoreboard is the single synchronisation point
across the three agents that write DMEM, and program order covers the one case
it cannot (\S\S\ref{sec:fabric-pipe}--\ref{sec:fabric-recycle}); and every
violation leaving an operand absent halts at a diagnostic state rather than
corrupting silently (\S\ref{sec:fail-stop}).

\subsection{Topology as a Runtime Parameter}\label{sec:fabric-topo}

Two compiler-loaded per-router tables parameterise the network. The
\emph{adjacency table} maps $(\text{router},\text{port}) \to (\text{target
router},\text{target port}) \mid \sv{ADJ\_DISCONNECTED}$; the \emph{routing
table} maps $(\text{router},\text{destination}) \to \text{output port}$. Both
are written through a configuration interface before \sv{program\_start}. A
single \sv{noc\_system} module supports the whole family $\T$; port~0 is
reserved for the local network interface on every router, the one structural
convention independent of topology. Adding a topology therefore requires a
Python classmethod that emits the two tables and no Verilog change: the
compiler ships six families (linear, ring, 2D mesh, 2D torus, fat-tree,
hypercube) with $O(1)$ analytical shortest paths and a BFS fallback at $O(G)$
per source for custom networks.

The binding ceiling on cluster size is the width of that configuration
interface rather than a design parameter. Adjacency writes carry a
\RouterIdBits-bit router id whose top code is the disconnected sentinel, so
ids are addressable to \RouterIdMax{} and a configuration above that aliases
silently --- which is exactly what defeats one instance of the suite
(\S\ref{sec:limitations}, L0). \sv{MAX\_ROUTERS} and \sv{MAX\_PORTS} are
declared in the packages and referenced by no module; they enforce nothing,
and we say so because a reader auditing the RTL for a cluster-size bound will
find them first.

\subsection{Packet Format and Reduction ISA}\label{sec:fabric-isa}

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\input{figures/variants/f04_fabric/a}
\caption{The fabric, traced along the path one 64-bit operand actually takes:
  a \texttt{SEND} on PE~3 forms a 96-bit single flit, the network interface
  merges the two compute-node links into one injection FIFO, the router
  resolves the egress port from its compiler-loaded route table, and on
  arrival the PIU --- not a \texttt{RECV} instruction, of which there is none
  --- checks \sv{dest\_gpu\_id} and writes DMEM itself, dropping and returning
  credit on a mismatch (\textsf{F-misroute}). The one thing to take from it is
  the last two steps: the scoreboard is the single source of truth for ``data
  present at address $a$'' across all three agents that write DMEM (PIU, GCI,
  FSM writeback), and \textsf{DE} holds the dependent \texttt{COMPUTE} until
  both operand bits are set, so a scoreboard-gated read is race-free against
  arrival time. The write arbiter's GCI retry latch is why no write is
  silently dropped, and \S\ref{sec:fabric-recycle} shows the latch is
  necessary for the \emph{value}, not only for liveness.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure}

\begin{table}[!t]
\caption{The four live opcodes. Opcodes $\geq \sv{4'h4}$, other than the one
  reserved slot, trap to \texttt{P\_ERROR} immediately.}
\label{tab:isa}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\ }l@{\ }p{5.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Mnemonic}    & \textbf{Code}  & \textbf{Effect} \\
\midrule
\texttt{NOP}         & \sv{4'h0}      & Consume one slot. \\
\texttt{GENERATE}    & \sv{4'h1}      & Fetch a leaf into \texttt{DMEM[dest]} via the GCI interface; set \texttt{scoreboard[dest]}. \\
\texttt{COMPUTE}     & \sv{4'h2}      & Read \texttt{DMEM[addr\_a]}, \texttt{DMEM[addr\_b]} (scoreboard-gated), write $\texttt{alu\_op}(a,b)$ to \texttt{DMEM[dest]}, set \texttt{scoreboard[dest]}. \\
\texttt{SEND}        & \sv{4'h3}      & Enqueue an RDMA-push packet with payload \texttt{DMEM[src]} to $(\text{dest\_gpu},\text{target\_addr})$ on \text{link}. \\
\texttt{OP\_RESERVED}& \sv{4'h4}      & Reserved for a future \texttt{BARRIER}/\texttt{RESET\_SB}. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Packets are 96-bit and single-flit, with the field layout given in
Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}. Bit $[64]$ is read by the router but written as the literal
\VcBitLiteral{} by the only packet-forming assignment in the design, so buffer
occupancy cannot be perturbed by the payload and the cycle counts we report are
value-agnostic by construction; \S\ref{sec:noc-route} says what that costs. The
instruction word is 64 bits,
\[
  \underbrace{\mathtt{opcode}}_{4}
  \|\underbrace{\mathtt{aux}}_{4}
  \|\underbrace{\mathtt{dest}}_{16}
  \|\underbrace{\mathtt{addr\_a}}_{16}
  \|\underbrace{\mathtt{addr\_b}}_{16}
  \|\underbrace{\mathtt{reserved}}_{8}\ \text{bits},
\]
with four live opcodes (Table~\ref{tab:isa}). Two source fields are mandatory
because \texttt{COMPUTE} names both members of the operand pair the ABI
binds; that is the ISA-level expression of Def.~\ref{def:opbind}. For
\texttt{SEND}, \sv{dest} is the \emph{destination-side} DMEM address carried
as \texttt{target\_addr} in the packet, \sv{addr\_a} the local source and
\sv{addr\_b} the destination PE. Egress port is deliberately \emph{not} an
instruction field: no small fixed field could address a router's egress
ports, which range to $P = \RadixMax$ across our suite
(\S\ref{sec:resource}), so the port is resolved in hardware by the emitting
router's route-table lookup. That single decision is what keeps topology a
configuration input rather than a property of the emitted code: the
instruction stream names logical destinations, and only the adjacency and
routing tables name the network.

The identity slot \texttt{DMEM[0]} is realised by resetting DMEM to all-zero
with \texttt{scoreboard[0]} set --- zero being the identity for ADD, FADD, OR
and XOR --- so that asymmetric trees or variable-arity reductions could supply
an identity operand without an ISA change. It is unread here.

\subsection{Pipeline, Scoreboard and Forwarding}\label{sec:fabric-pipe}

Each PE runs the three-stage pipeline of Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}, with
\textsf{EX} additionally stalling on back-pressure or a write collision. The
DMEM read path carries a
two-level write-to-read forwarding network realising \textsf{F-fw}: level~1
forwards a cycle-$t$ write to a cycle-$(t{+}1)$ read of the same address, the
back-to-back \texttt{COMPUTE} case; level~2 forwards across a single
intervening stall, where the one-cycle forward has expired before the read
settles. Given the pipeline depth and the scoreboard's one-cycle gate the two
levels exhaust the races.

Because presence is decided in one place
independently of which port delivered the data, a scoreboard-gated read is
structurally race-free against remote arrival --- the fabric never needs to
know \emph{when} a packet lands, only that it has.

\subsection{Why the Scoreboard Alone Is Not Enough}\label{sec:fabric-recycle}

The single-writer discipline \textsf{C-sw} is scoped to receive buffers, and
that scoping is the part of the design most easily misread, so we state what
covers the rest. The allocator returns a child's slot to a free list once its
parent has consumed it (\S\ref{sec:compiler}), so a \emph{local temporary}
can be written more than once per program. Read against a scoreboard bit that
is never cleared, that looks unsafe: the second writer finds the bit already
set. Nor is reuse a corner case one could restrict the claim away from --- over
\RecycleConfigs{} compiled configurations we count \RecycleAddrs{} recycled
addresses and \RecycleEvents{} reuse events, and \emph{every} configuration
recycles.

It is safe, and there are exactly two cases, separated by how many readers of
the old value are still outstanding when the slot is rewritten. In
\RecycleZeroReaderPct{} of reuse events there are none: the last consumer has
retired and the slot was only then returned to the free list. In the
remaining \RecycleSelfReaderPct{} there is exactly one, and it is the very
\texttt{COMPUTE} that overwrites the slot, which under \textsf{F-inorder}
samples both operands at the \textsf{DE} read port strictly before writing
back in \textsf{EX}. Over the same configurations no reuse event has a
remaining reader other than the overwriting instruction and none has two, so
the two cases are exhaustive (\RecycleUnsafe{} unsafe events in
\RecycleEvents{}). The ordering is supplied by program order on one PE, not
by the scoreboard. The scoreboard exists for the one case program order
cannot cover --- a value written by a \emph{different} PE, whose arrival time
is a function of routing and contention --- and those destinations are
precisely the receive buffers, which are never recycled. We verified the
separation directly on the emitted images: the recycled and the
remotely-written address sets never intersect.

One sub-case of the second is not covered by program order either, and it is
why \textsf{F-gci-haz} and \textsf{F-arb} are hypotheses of
Claim~\ref{claim:1} rather than liveness conveniences. \texttt{GENERATE} is
asynchronous: the instruction asserts \sv{gci\_start} in \textsf{EX} and the
GCI agent commits the leaf $\GciLatency$ or more cycles later, against a
compiler-emitted gap of \GciGapMin{} cycles at minimum and \GciGapMedian{} at
the median. \GenRecycledPct{} of \texttt{GENERATE}s (\GenRecycled{} of
\GenTotal{}) target a \emph{recycled} slot whose bit is already set by the
previous writer, and every one of them is followed by a read of that slot; the
scoreboard therefore cannot stall the consumer and cannot be what makes them
safe. The in-flight interlock \textsf{F-gci-haz}, which stalls in \textsf{DE}
any \texttt{COMPUTE} or \texttt{SEND} naming a pending destination, is what
makes them safe. The RTL comment calls that interlock belt-and-braces with
the scoreboard; it is not.

\textsf{F-arb} completes the pair. The DMEM write arbiter is strict-priority
$\mathrm{PIU} > \mathrm{GCI} > \mathrm{FSM}$ --- PIU always wins, preserving
the RDMA-push semantic that incoming data is never blocked --- with a GCI
\emph{retry latch}: when a GCI completion collides with a PIU write in the
same cycle the arbiter drops the GCI write, and the latch captures the
pending value and re-asserts it until accepted. Without the latch the leaf
value is silently lost while the PIU still sets the presence bit, and the
next \texttt{COMPUTE} reads a wrong leaf and produces a wrong root with no
diagnostic. Remove either mechanism and the consumer reads a stale value,
with no stall and no error: they are necessary for the value, not merely for
liveness, which is the reason both appear in Claim~\ref{claim:1}'s hypothesis
list where a reader might expect only \textsf{F-sb-gate}.

\subsection{Fail-Stop Discipline}\label{sec:fail-stop}

The PIU's header check against the local PE (Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}) is what
discards a misrouted packet --- a routing-table bug, a corrupted packet, a
torn adjacency --- rather than writing it (\textsf{F-misroute}). The drop and
the credit return are real hardware; the misroute flag itself is an internal signal with no reader and no
module port, so a misroute is observable only through the liveness failure it
causes. That is the intended shape: a bad routing table leaves the
destination's presence bit clear, its dependent \texttt{COMPUTE} stalls, and
the run halts with a recorded program counter instead of returning a
different number.

Three detectors run in the \texttt{P\_RUN} state. The watchdog fires after
$\sv{WATCHDOG\_MAX} = \WatchdogMax$ cycles with no instruction retired; a
stall timer fires after $\sv{TIMEOUT\_MAX} = 10{,}000$ cycles of continuous
\textsf{EX} stall; and any opcode above the reserved slot traps immediately.
Each raises \texttt{P\_ERROR} with \sv{error\_pc} and \sv{error\_state} for
post-mortem. The termination outcomes are therefore (i) a correct result,
(ii) \texttt{P\_ERROR} with diagnostic context, or (iii) a watchdog timeout
with the same context, and no configuration in the campaign produced a
fourth. We do not claim a fourth is impossible: Remark~\ref{rem:cmem} gives
the one construction --- an image over the \textsf{C-mem} budget --- that
defeats the presence gate instead of tripping it.

\subsection{Flow Control, Routing, and Deadlock}\label{sec:noc-route}

Each input port carries \NumVcs{} virtual channels and every emitted testbench
sizes router FIFOs at \BufDepthSim{} flits, overriding the RTL default of
\BufDepthRtl. Per-link credit-based flow control prevents ingress overflow,
with credit returns serialised through a pending-credit register that drains
one pulse per cycle; that register is \CreditCtrBits{} bits wide and wraps
only on a backlog of \CreditCtrWrap, which requires two virtual channels to be
read in one cycle. It never happens here, for the reason the next paragraph
gives, and its value is provably zero in every reported cycle.

\emph{One channel, and no escape.} The router reads bit $[64]$ as a VC
selector but nothing writes it: the field is a constant in the only
packet-forming assignment, the ISA has no VC field, and the compiler contains
no virtual-channel logic, so every packet in every reported run travels on
\sv{VC0}. Nor could the second channel serve as an escape channel if the
compiler did assign one --- the router's egress buffer is a single FIFO per
port shared across VCs, so the two channels are coupled at the output whatever
the header says.

\emph{What discharges \textsf{C-route}, and what does not.} The compiler
computes routing tables by greedy minimal-distance search over the adjacency
list; they are not dimension-ordered. That construction gives exactly what
\textsf{C-route} claims: every emitted path terminates at the destination
named in the header and visits no router twice. It does not give an acyclic
channel-dependency graph in the sense of Dally and
Seitz~\cite{dally1987deadlock}. Built directly from the emitted tables, the CDG
contains cycles on every ring instance (cycle length $G$, the textbook
bidirectional-ring cycle) and on every torus instance (length
\CdgTorusCycLo--\CdgTorusCycHi); it is acyclic on linear, mesh, hypercube and
fat-tree at every suite size. We therefore claim no deadlock-freedom property
on cyclic topologies. Deadlock is possible in principle, and the fabric
converts it into a fail-stop rather than a wrong answer: a deadlocked PE
retires nothing, the watchdog fires, and Property~\ref{prop:2} applies. That
is where most of the campaign's non-settling runs come from
(\S\ref{sec:limitations}, L0a). A compiler-side dimension-ordered pass with a
VC-escape assignment, and a per-VC egress buffer to make that escape real,
are the two changes a production deployment would need; neither can change a
bit result, only whether the run terminates.

A second silent-drop channel has the same shape and the same bound. The
emitted testbenches give the compute node's link to the network interface
\NiCredits{} credits against an \NiFifoDepth-entry injection FIFO, so a
sufficiently long injection burst would overflow the FIFO and the packet
would be discarded with no flag. The presence gate bounds the damage exactly
as above: a lost \texttt{SEND} leaves the destination's bit clear, the
dependent \texttt{COMPUTE} stalls, the watchdog fires. A drop can cost
termination and never correctness, which is why no passing run can contain
one.

\subsection{Resource Envelope}\label{sec:resource}


Router cost is dominated by radix, and radix is a property of the topology
rather than a constant of the design: the live parameter is
\sv{PORTS\_PER\_RTR}, emitted per instance and read back out of every generated
testbench rather than assumed. It spans \RadixMin--\RadixMax{} ports across the
suite --- linear and ring at \RadixMin, mesh and torus at $P = \RadixLo$,
hypercube reaching $P = \RadixHc$ at $G = 1024$, fat-tree reaching
$P = \RadixMax$ at $G = 4096$ (\RadixMaxInst, \RadixMaxRouters{} routers) ---
and on every topology at every size the emitted adjacency table wires exactly
that many ports. Because the crossbar term is $O(P^2)$, a single fixed-radix
estimate is wrong by more than an order of magnitude at the top of that range,
so we report the envelope as a function of $P$ at a fixed route-table depth of
$G = 4096$, counting routing table, ingress and egress FIFOs and crossbar as
storage-equivalent bits and excluding link drivers, clocking, arbiter logic and
I/O. A fat-tree router is \RouterBlowup$\times$ a mesh
router (\RouterBitsFt{} bits against \RouterBitsLo), \XbarShareFt{} of it
crossbar (\XbarBitsFt{} bits); aggregated over $4096$ routers that is
${\approx}\AggLoMbit$~Mbit at $P = \RadixLo$ against ${\approx}\AggFtMbit$~Mbit
for \RadixMaxInst{} --- the regime in which a flat crossbar stops being the right
structure and a hierarchical or input-queued switch is the standard answer. We
report the flat figure because it is what we simulated.

Per-PE memory is topology-independent but only half fixed: DMEM is
$\DmemDepth \times 64$ on every instance, while IMEM is elaborated to the next
power of two above that instance's longest per-PE program, \ImemDepthLo{} to
\ImemDepthHi{} entries across the suite. We price the $\DmemDepth \times 64$
case for both --- \PerPEBits{} bits per PE, ${\approx}\AggPEMbit$~Mbit over
$G = 4096$ --- as a design target, not as a measurement of what every run
instantiated. All of these are RTL-level counts from a prototype whose ALU is
combinational: we have run no synthesis and report no $F_{\max}$, slack,
utilisation or power anywhere in this paper.

\subsection{The Adder, and a Defect Only an External Standard Found}
\label{sec:fabric-fadd}

\begin{figure}[!tb]
\centering
\input{figures/variants/f12_fp64_defect/a}
\caption{The effective-subtraction defect and its repair, on the adder
  datapath. The alignment tail was recorded in \sv{sticky} but never borrowed
  from the difference, and the \emph{addition} rounding rule was then applied
  to the result. The one thing to take from it is why the fix is three edits
  and not one: \sv{sticky} threads every stage, so borrowing the tail changes
  what the renormalising shift and the final rounding decision mean. Edit~2
  alone --- the obvious one-line patch --- still leaves \FpPartialPct{} of
  effective subtractions wrong, which is why correctness here is established
  by the sweep beside its negative control and not by the patch.}
\label{fig:fp64defect}
\end{figure}

The adder we first submitted did not implement round-to-nearest-even on
effective subtraction, and how it escaped is more useful than the patch.
Fig.~\ref{fig:fp64defect} gives the mechanism on the datapath. Scored against
the host's correctly-rounded addition the defect fires on \FpBandLo--\FpBandHi{} of
opposite-signed pairs whose exponents differ by \FpBandDeLo{} to
\FpBandDeHi{} binades, and on \emph{every} such pair at a difference of
exactly \FpFullDe{}.

The repair takes the three coordinated edits marked in
Fig.~\ref{fig:fp64defect}. Stopping after the borrow, the obvious one-line
fix, leaves a $-1$~ulp residual on \FpPartialPct{} of effective subtractions
(\FpPartialErrors{} of \FpPartialVectors{} in a three-variant sweep),
concentrated at exponent separations of \FpPartialDeLo--\FpPartialDeHi{}
binades. A partial repair here looks plausible and is wrong, which is why what
establishes correctness is the verification and not the patch. On a two-directional binade sweep plus
a uniform random sample the repaired adder agrees with correctly-rounded
IEEE~754 addition on all \FpAcceptVectors{} vectors (\FpAcceptErrors{}
errors) and the repaired software oracle agrees with it bit for bit on the
same set (\FpAcceptMismatch{} mismatches); over the wider host-FPU sweep the
figure is \FpSweepErrors{} of \FpSweepVectors{}. The negative control fires:
the as-submitted pair fails the same test on \FpCtrlErrors{} of
\FpCtrlVectors{} vectors.

No number in this paper moves, and we checked that rather than argued it:
replaying the emitted reduction order under the as-submitted and the repaired
oracle over \FpScopeGvals{} worker counts from \FpScopeGLo{} to \FpScopeGHi{}
moves \FpScopeMoved{} roots and encounters \FpScopeMixed{} mixed-sign
additions, while the guard's own injected-adder control detects
\FpScopeMutant{}. The reason it moves nothing is the reason the campaign
could never have found it, and that is L13's subject
(\S\ref{sec:limitations}) rather than an erratum.

\subsection{What the Fabric Does Not Do}\label{sec:fabric-lim}

\emph{Head-of-line blocking.} The router is store-and-forward with a single
FIFO per VC; under tree-reduction traffic the root-incident links queue up to
$\lceil \log_2 G\rceil$ merge waves, and absolute cycle counts slew at $G \geq
1024$ on ring and torus because of it. Wormhole forwarding is a planned
extension and does not touch the ABI.

\emph{Single clock domain.} A multi-chiplet deployment at $G = 4096$ would
need asynchronous FIFOs on inter-chiplet links, changing credit round-trip
latencies but not the bit result.

\emph{Validated at one point of a parameterised design, and the unused halves
are where the defects are.} The fabric instantiates \NumVcs{} virtual
channels, two compute-node links and $k/2$ fat-tree core switches; the
compiler uses one of each. The credit backlog register above can only
overflow on a two-VC read; the network interface's injection race can only
fire on the second link; and for $k \geq 4$ the fat-tree emitter assigns
pod-to-core ports above the declared radix, which the fabric discards, so the
elaborated network uses a single core switch. Every emitted route is valid on
that network and the surplus cores carry no traffic --- but the analytic lower
bound $\Omega$ (\S\ref{sec:method}) min-cuts the intended edge set, so the
fat-tree $\Omega$ ratios we report are computed against a \emph{more} capable
network than the one simulated. That is an understatement of our own
performance, not a flattery, and we state it as one caveat on the RTL rather
than as three separate errata.

\emph{Soft-enforced single-writer.} \textsf{C-sw} is discharged by a
compile-time post-condition over the emitted image, not by a hardware refusal
of a second write to an already-set slot. A one-line RTL extension --- raise
\texttt{P\_ERROR} on a scoreboard transition from $1$ to $1$ --- would harden
it into a fabric-side guarantee.

\section{The Compiler}\label{sec:compiler}
% =====================================================================

  ran rather than the one the released tool can express. The $18\times10$
  $(\text{S2},\text{S3})$ face is enumerated exhaustively on every instance
  (\S\ref{sec:method}); S4 is the axis the campaign does not cover
  (\S\ref{sec:limitations}).}
\label{tab:stages}
\centering
\footnotesize
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\ \ }r@{\ \ }p{4.35cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Pass} & \textbf{Alt.} & \textbf{Status in the reported campaign} \\
\midrule
S0\ \ lower bound $\Omega$        & --  & a reported metric, not a construction step (\S\ref{sec:method}) \\
S1\ \ $\FBT(N)$ instantiation     & 1   & ran; fixes the binding of Defs.~\ref{def:opbind}--\ref{def:leafbind} \\

S2.5 connectivity repair          & 1   & never invoked; not load-bearing (below) \\
